summary: Monaco, the guess everyone makes, is now #1 and San Marino #2, from the UN's own note on its table. Japan and Switzerland come fast, Andorra and South Korea take thought, and the Nordics are the traps.
reasons: Fixed (data agent, Nov 13): Monaco 86.37 and San Marino 85.71 rank from the UN note on the page (build option textRows, which fails if the page stops saying it). Top 10: Monaco, San Marino, Japan, South Korea, Andorra, Switzerland, Australia, Singapore, Italy, Spain; France #11, Norway #12. Both new answers have facts, and Japan's no longer claims first place (Hong Kong, a territory, tops the UN table).

Replayed after the fix: casual 7 (Japan, Switzerland, Monaco, Singapore, Australia, Italy, Spain; lives on Norway #12, Sweden #14, Iceland #16, Canada #17, France #11). Three other honest orders land 7, 7 and 8. Only an order that leads with five Nordic countries collapses (2). Fan 10 in 12 guesses, Hong Kong and Liechtenstein free.
Liechtenstein stays free: the page gives it no UN figure. The UN's own data (WPP 2024) gives 83.63 for 2023, below Spain's 83.67, so the top 10 is right without it and the prompt needs no caveat.
Fairness stays 3: with Norway out of the top 10 all five Nordics are near misses with figures. They teach, but they end most games.

Too close to happiest-countries for one week: the same well-off countries, with the Nordics as the gimmes there and the traps here. Run them at least a week apart, and keep both away from gdp-per-capita.
fixes: Coordinator, not a rebuild: 'hong kong' reads 'Hong kong isn't in this ranking. No life lost.' That's untrue (it is the table's #1), and it echoes the typed casing ('Hong kong'). A territory the list leaves out needs a line like 'Hong Kong isn't a country here.', and the line should use the name's own casing.
